subject: MultiGroup Analysis SEM Fixing Means in Group 1 but not Group 2 or 3

messages.author: 8ec9822ca0607e51
messages.subject: MultiGroup Analysis SEM Fixing Means in Group 1 but not Group 2 or 3
parts:
Please can you help?

How do I release some of the restrictions in my code: 

(a) the means of the latent variables (and model variables that are only measured by 1 item) should be fixed to 0 in group  1 but free in group 2 and 3 so that differences between groups can be detected. (I  only have three groups in total)

(b) the regression coefficients should be free for the groups so that you can test if there are differences. 

(c) loadings on latent variables and intercepts of indicators for latent variables should be fixed (-> measurement invariance), if possible also the residual variances of the indicator variables, but this can be relaxed. 

Here is the code.

mltsem_m4 <- '
        #? measrement part
        pa =~ Q64_1 + Q66_1
        mg_intf =~ Q35_1 #? single indicator latent var
        Q35_1 ~~ 0 * Q35_1 #? x1  ~~ err.var * x1 (assumed err.var = 0) [err.var = (1 - alpha) * var]
        mg1_intf =~ Q61_1 #? single indicator latent var
        Q61_1 ~~ 0 * Q61_1 #? x1  ~~ err.var * x1 (assumed err.var = 0) [err.var = (1 - alpha) * var]
        mg2_intf =~ Q62 #? single indicator latent var
        Q62 ~~ 0 * Q62 #? x1  ~~ err.var * x1 (assumed err.var = 0) [err.var = (1 - alpha) * var]
        #? structural part
        pa ~ mg_intf + mg1_intf + mg2_intf
 '
mltsem9 <- sem(mltsem_m4, data=data_1, group = "gWP4", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "residual.covariances", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances", "regressions")) #? multiple group sem, configural model
summary(mltsem9, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
anova(mltsem9, mltsem8)
modindices(mltsem9)

messages.subject: Re: MultiGroup Analysis SEM Fixing Means in Group 1 but not Group 2 or 3
parts:
Robert,
  My impression is that it is a fairly easy to begin with convenience features and then run into trouble specifying a more complicated model.  My suggestion is to (a) first write out the model in algebra or a full path diagram with all parameters shown, (b) then specify the model in lavaan using the lavaan() function and no convenience parameters, (c) only then, and optionally, modify the script to incorporate convenience functions and convenience parameters.

  Here is a script that illustrates some of the constraints that you describe.  Note that there is an important distinction between fixed parameters (e.g., zero means) and constrained parameters (e.g., invariant across groups). The key bit of syntax is the use of vectors constructed with the c() function as parameter modifiers.  In your case, they will have a length of three.  NA frees a parameter.


HS.model <- '
  # Loadings
  visual  =~ 1*x1 + x2 + c(l1, l1)*x3 # x3 loading equality constraint
  textual =~ 1*x4 + x5 + x6
  speed   =~ 1*x7 + x8 + x9

  # Variances
  visual~~visual
  textual~~textual
  speed~~speed
  x1~~x1
  x2~~x2
  x3~~x3
  x4~~x4
  x5~~x5
  x6~~x6
  x7~~x7
  x8~~x8
  x9~~x9

  # Regressions
  speed ~ visual + c(b1,b1)*textual #equality constraint on second regression weight
 
  # Means
  visual ~ c(0, NA)*1 # fixed to zero in first group
  textual ~ c(0, NA)*1
  speed   ~ c(0, NA)*1

  # intercepts
  x1 ~ c(i1,i1)*1 # equality constraint
  x2 ~ c(i2,i2)*1
  x3 ~ c(i3,i3)*1
  x4 ~ c(i4,i4)*1
  x5 ~ c(i5,i5)*1
  x6 ~ c(i6,i6)*1
  x7 ~ c(i7,i7)*1
  x8 ~ c(i8,i8)*1
  x9 ~ c(i9,i9)*1  


' # end HS.model

fit <- lavaan(HS.model,
           data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
           group = "school")

           
summary(fit)

Keith
